summary: ICMP and UDP filtering at customer edge causes DoT/DoH fallback loop and intermittent gRPC streaming stalls on private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent model artifact download failures and GRPC streaming resets from their private deployment. Failures cluster around bulk inference jobs and long-lived streams.

Impact:
- Multiple inference requests returning 502/504 or streaming disconnects for a subset of serving nodes for ~10-30s every 5-20 minutes.
- High error rates during model pulls (~10-15% of downloads) when scale-up events occur.
- Customer workload (batch scoring) experiencing timeouts and downstream job failures.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) peered with Redwood control plane.
- Edge: Palo Alto SD-WAN appliance + corporate firewall policy.
- Observed region: prod/us-east-1.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Trigger parallel model pulls by scaling serving nodes (e.g., deploy new model or scale replica count).
2) Start long-lived streaming sessions to same serving nodes (chat/stream).
3) After ~1-2 minutes of sustained parallel activity, some streams drop and artifact downloads stall/retry.

Observed behavior:
- tcpdump on serving node shows repeated ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages followed by apparent UDP 53 timeouts.
- Local resolver on customer forwarder attempts DoH (443) then DoT (853) then plain UDP 53 in fallback order; when UDP 53 is blocked the resolver retries DoT/DoH but the corporate TLS inspection rewrites SNI causing TLS handshake failures.
- Control-plane auth calls timeout intermittently; serving nodes enter backoff and retry model fetches, causing 503s at client side.
- GRPC streams see RST/GoAway events aligned with the time windows of resolver churn and PMTU probes.

Expected behavior:
- DNS resolution and artifact fetches should succeed without blackholing during PMTU discovery or DoH/DoT fallback.

Logs / artifacts provided:
- tcpdump pcap from customer edge (attached in support portal) showing ICMP type 3 code 4 (frag needed) packets and subsequent retransmits.
- Resolver logs (unbound) showing repeated retries between DoH/DoT/UDP and TLS alert 40 (handshake failure) from inspection device.
- Serving node system logs showing repeated "artifact fetch retry" messages and gRPC stream reset counters increasing.

Customer-provided context:
- Firewall team recently deployed strict egress policy that blocks UDP 53 and rate-limits ICMP to 1 pps per prefix for security.
- SD-WAN vendor recently enabled MSS clamping on some tunnels.
comments: 2026-03-14 15:08 - Support (Aisha Njoroge): Acknowledged. I've collected initial tcpdump and resolver logs from the customer. Escalating to SRE/networking. (sla: P1)

2026-03-14 15:27 - SRE (Mateo Alvarez): Observed PMTU ICMP frag-needed followed by resolver jumping through DoH/DoT fallback. Hypothesis: blocking UDP 53 combined with ICMP rate-limiting causes PMTU discovery to fail and pushes resolver into TLS-based flows which are mangled by the TLS inspection box.

2026-03-14 16:12 - Customer (NetOps, Sara Li): Confirmed we recently tightened egress rules and limit ICMP due to previous amplification attacks. We can temporarily allow UDP 53 and increase ICMP allowance for testing. Requesting guidance on safe config to unblock production.

2026-03-14 17:02 - Support (Aisha Njoroge): Requested customer temporarily allow outbound UDP/53 to Redwoods control plane and allow ICMP frag-needed messages between serving subnets and their edge for 1 hour. Also suggested bypassing TLS inspection for traffic to redwood-inference endpoints (whitelist).
2026-03-15 09:40 - SRE (Mateo Alvarez): Customer performed the temporary allow. Errors dropped to baseline and artifact pulls completed. Need coordinated long-term mitigation plan.

2026-03-15 11:05 - Customer (Sara Li): We'll implement whitelist for redwood domains and relax ICMP rate-limit. Please provide recommended firewall rules and a runbook entry so SOC can approve change.
2026-03-15 14:30 - Support (Aisha Njoroge): Preparing runbook & recommended firewall policy. Will include steps for whitelist, ICMP allowances, and verification commands.
investigation_notes: SRE reproduced pattern in lab with controlled MTU and an HTTP/TLS-inspecting proxy: when UDP 53 is blocked and ICMP frag-needed is rate-limited, client resolvers prefer DoH/DoT which then fail due to SNI rewrite by TLS inspection, causing unresolved hostnames and stalled artifact fetches.

tcpdump snippet: multiple ICMP type 3 code 4 from upstream router. Subsequent artifact fetchs trigger retransmit, then TLS handshake TLSv1.3 alerts from inspection device referencing bad SNI. PCAP correlates to gRPC stream resets timeline.

Customer edge shows MSS clamping on SD-WAN tunnel (MSS set to 1200) which combined with dropped ICMP prevents PMTU negotiation, increasing fragmentation of TLS records and triggering inspection failures.
No evidence that Redwood serving runtime is dropping packets; problem reproduces only when edge policies block UDP 53 and rate-limit ICMP below recommended levels.
Related internal ticket INT-4421 opened to track adding clearer network requirements to private-deploy quickstart and to add checks in the agent's preflight to warn on blocked UDP/ICMP behavior.
resolution: Workaround (customer applied 2026-03-15 09:30): Temporarily allow outbound UDP/53 to the control-plane resolver IP ranges and increase ICMP frag-needed allowance to 10 pps between serving subnets and edge for 24 hours. Disable TLS inspection/whitelist for redwood-inference endpoints. Result: errors reduced to baseline and artifact fetch success rate returned to normal.

Permanent recommendations provided to customer:
- Whitelist redwood control-plane and artifact S3 endpoints on firewall/inspection device (include IP ranges and SANs provided in separate secure doc).
- Allow ICMP type 3 code 4 between serving subnets and edge so PMTU discovery works; if policy prohibits full ICMP, permit at least frag-needed for the relevant prefixes.
- Allow UDP/53 to upstream resolvers or configure a trusted resolver inside VPC that forwards with UDP preserved.
- Avoid in-line TLS inspection for traffic to model-artifact hosts (breaks DoT/DoH heuristics).
- Review SD-WAN MSS clamping settings; align MSS to allow TLS record sizes (>=1400) or permit PMTU discovery to adjust.

Follow-ups:\n- INT-4421: Add explicit network preflight checks to Redwood private-deploy agent to detect blocked UDP53 and suppressed ICMP and surface warnings during install.\n- Create KB article for customers on \"Network requirements for Private Deploy: DNS, ICMP, PMTU and TLS inspection\" and add to onboarding checklist.
Status: Mitigated (customer applied temporary changes). Awaiting long-term policy change and confirmation from SOC.
